name: Cyrus (Persian king)
title: The Lord's anointed shepherd
summary: Cyrus the Great was the founder of the Persian Empire and the conqueror of Babylon in 539 BC. He is remarkable in biblical history because God called him his 'anointed' and used him to free the Jews from the Babylonian captivity and allow the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Prophesied by name by Isaiah
keyEvents.description: More than 150 years before Cyrus's birth, Isaiah prophesied about him by name, calling him the Lord's shepherd and anointed one who would rebuild Jerusalem and the temple.

keyEvents.title: The conquest of Babylon
keyEvents.description: Cyrus conquered Babylon in 539 BC without major fighting, fulfilling prophecies about Babylon's fall and opening the way for the Jews' release.

keyEvents.title: Decree on the return of the Jews
keyEvents.description: In his first year of ruling over Babylon, Cyrus issued a decree allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.

keyEvents.title: Return of the Temple Articles
keyEvents.description: Cyrus ordered that the holy vessels and articles which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem should be returned to the Jews.

keyEvents.title: Funding for the Temple Construction
keyEvents.description: Cyrus gave orders that the costs for rebuilding the temple should be covered by the royal treasury, and he set the dimensions of the building.
